# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The embossed instruction is tactile, so I can read it: no wire should be cut. The wire contents, display, and light are unknown to me. I need Mute to use the next round to obtain the Deaf monkey’s visual observations and relay the manual’s relevant procedure. I will not act on the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel an embossed instruction: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I will not cut anything. Please use the next round to have Deaf report every visible display, light, colour, and wire marking through gestures, then tell me what the manual requires.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see display 0, red light, and an embossed warning: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. The wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The visual observations are now available: display 0, red light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. They agree with the tactile warning, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I need the manual’s rule for this combination before doing anything; I will ask Mute to provide it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I now know the bomb shows display 0, a red light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The tactile warning still says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. What does the manual require for this exact combination?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled four gestures in order: pinching hand, index pointing up, index pointing at you, handshake. Bomb remains display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

I still do not know what the four gestures mean; descriptions of gestures are not enough without the manual’s code. The warning independently rules out every cutting action, so I will not guess. I need Mute to make the manual’s required outcome explicit through the Deaf monkey, who can observe Mute’s gestures and tell me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received four gestures but do not know their meaning. Please signal the manual's required action or result in a clearly defined sequence that Deaf can report to me, including whether any wire must be cut. The tactile warning says no wire may be cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gesture sequence: index pointing at you, pinching hand, index pointing up, index pointing right. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

The new gestures still have no established meaning for me, so I cannot safely decode them. The only reliable facts remain display 0, red light, and the tactile prohibition against cutting any wire. I need the manual’s instruction stated in ordinary speech, rather than encoded gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the relevant manual instruction aloud in plain words, including the exact safe action for display 0 and red light. Do not encode it with gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled: folded-hands prayer, pinching hand, index pointing up, index pointing up.

The reported gestures still have no agreed code, so they cannot safely communicate the manual’s instruction. I will establish an explicit code with Mute: one gesture will identify the required action, while the Deaf monkey can report which gesture was displayed. Since the tactile warning forbids cutting, I expect the safe result to be waiting, but I will verify it rather than assume.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one gesture in your next turn to report the manual's required action. Code: 🙏 means wait and do not touch; ☝ means cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3. Deaf will report which gesture you used, and I will decode it.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gestures, in order: index pointing at you, index pointing upward with one finger, pinching hand. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

The latest signal does not follow the one-gesture code: it contains three gestures, so it does not identify a wire or authorize cutting one. The tactile warning still explicitly forbids cutting, and no safe action has been established. I will continue to avoid touching the bomb and ask Mute to send exactly the agreed wait signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your latest signal had three gestures, so I cannot decode it under our agreed code. Please send exactly one gesture: 🙏 means WAIT and DO NOT TOUCH. Do not signal any wire-cut instruction unless the manual explicitly overrides the embossed warning.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture is ?: one index finger pointing upward. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

The single gesture is ☝, which under the code I proposed would mean “cut wire 1.” However, the tactile warning directly says “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and no communicated manual instruction can override that warning. I will not cut wire 1; I need the manual instruction conveyed in plain speech or a signal explicitly confirming that waiting is safe.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received ☝, which would mean cut wire 1 under my code, but that conflicts with the tactile warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I will not cut. Please state the manual instruction in plain speech, and do not use gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signalled exactly one gesture: ?, index finger pointing upward. No bomb state change: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

The repeated ☝ signal would mean “cut wire 1” under the code I supplied, but it conflicts with the directly tactile instruction “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” I will trust the unambiguous instruction on the bomb and take no cutting action. No safe cut is established.

```text
wait()
```
